title: Othello presented by Bedlam at the West End Theatre #othello #bedlamt...
transcript: Is this four-person Shakespeare production a bold creative choice, or just a recession indicator? Both can be true, but I'll give it the benefit of the doubt. Othello is a potent tragedy about jealousy, betrayal, and prejudice, and this bare production from Bedlam keenly puts these emotional experiences under a microscope. With a small cast, there's obviously some role doubling — you may spend the first bit just figuring out who's who. This will be easier if you already know the story, but you'll still be able to get the plot regardless, at least in broad strokes. Othello is far from my favorite tragedy, but I thought it was a great vehicle for these actors who give richly psychological performances and a refreshing cadence that I found modern but not jarring. Ryan Quinn as Othello is especially fantastic, as is Susannah Hoffman in a crazy track that includes Desdemona and Cassio. It took me a while to get into Act 1, but Act 2 was intensely intimate and visceral, helped by a seating arrangement that both contains and is surrounded by the action. If you're not intimidated by a deconstructed production or an almost three hour run time, this one's worth checking out. With that another program for my collection.
